blocks.text: A gearbox shaft slides into its bearing with a push of the thumb in one batch and needs a hydraulic press in the next. Both batches were drawn to the same nominal size: the difference was how the limits on hole and shaft overlapped.

blocks.markdown: No two parts are made to exactly the same size, so a drawing gives **limits**: a largest and smallest permitted size. Hole and shaft **limits of size** decide whether the pair has clearance, interference or a mixture. The ISO system names a tolerance by a letter (the position of the zone relative to the nominal size: capitals for holes, lower case for shafts) and a number (the **IT grade**, the width of the zone: smaller number, tighter tolerance).

blocks.title: Fit
blocks.text: A **fit** is the relationship between a hole and a shaft of the same nominal size. **Clearance fit**: the shaft is always smaller than the hole. **Interference fit**: the shaft is always larger than the hole. **Transition fit**: depending on the actual sizes, either clearance or interference may result.

blocks.latex: C_{\max} = D_{\max} - d_{\min},\qquad C_{\min} = D_{\min} - d_{\max}
blocks.caption: Largest and smallest clearance from hole limits D and shaft limits d. A negative value is an interference of that size.

blocks.markdown: In the **hole-basis system** the hole has its lower deviation equal to zero (letter H) and the shaft zone moves to give the fit, so one drill and reamer size serves many fits. The preferred fits are named from the combination, such as H7/g6 (close running, clearance), H7/h6 (locational clearance), H7/k6 (locational transition) and H7/p6 (interference, press fit). The values below for 18 to 30 mm nominal size are typical, in millimetres.

blocks.caption: Typical limits (mm) for nominal sizes 18 to 30 mm, hole basis

blocks.title: A clearance fit, 25 H7/g6
blocks.prompt: Hole limits are 25.000 and 25.021 mm; shaft limits are 24.980 and 24.993 mm. Find the maximum and minimum clearance and classify.

steps.text: Largest clearance: largest hole minus smallest shaft.
Smallest clearance: smallest hole minus largest shaft.
Both are positive, so the shaft is always smaller than the hole.

blocks.answer: Maximum clearance 0.041 mm, minimum 0.007 mm: a clearance fit.

blocks.title: An interference fit, 25 H7/p6
blocks.prompt: Hole limits are 25.000 and 25.021 mm; shaft limits are 25.022 and 25.035 mm. Find the largest and smallest interference and classify.

steps.text: Largest interference: largest shaft minus smallest hole.
Smallest interference: smallest shaft minus largest hole.
Both are positive, so the shaft is always larger than the hole.

blocks.answer: Interference between 0.001 mm and 0.035 mm: an interference (press) fit.

blocks.markdown: **Classifying a fit from numbers.** Compute $C_{\max}$ and $C_{\min}$. If both are positive the fit is clearance. If both are negative it is interference. If $C_{\max}$ is positive and $C_{\min}$ negative it is a transition fit. **Selecting a fit** starts with the function: free running, accurate location, or fixed assembly.

blocks.title: Bearing seat
blocks.text: A rolling bearing inner ring on a rotating shaft needs a tight fit to prevent creep: a shaft in the k or m zone (typically k6) is a common choice, with the bearing outer ring in an H7 housing. The fit is chosen so the ring cannot turn on the shaft but can still be mounted without extreme force.

blocks.title: Sign errors
blocks.text: Interference is negative clearance. Subtract the right pair: largest hole minus smallest shaft gives the largest clearance, not the smallest.

points: Clearance, transition and interference fits come from comparing hole and shaft limits.
C_max = D_max - d_min and C_min = D_min - d_max; a negative result is interference.
Select the fit from the function, for example H7/k6 for a bearing seat on a shaft.

options.text: The shaft is always larger than the hole
The shaft is always smaller than the hole
Either clearance or interference can occur
The hole and shaft have the same limits

questions.correctOptionText: The shaft is always smaller than the hole
questions.explanation: A clearance fit has a positive gap for every pair of parts within limits. Larger shaft than hole defines interference; either defines transition.

questions.stem: In the hole-basis system, which statement about the hole is correct?

options.text: The lower deviation is zero (letter H)
The hole size is always smaller

questions.correctOptionText: The lower deviation is zero (letter H)

distractorRationale.a: That is the shaft basis h.

questions.explanation: In hole-basis fits the hole is H, with lower deviation zero, and the shaft is varied. This lets one hole tool serve many fits.

questions.stem: A hole has limits 40.000 mm and 40.025 mm. The mating shaft has limits 39.975 mm and 39.991 mm. Calculate the maximum clearance in mm.
questions.explanation: Maximum clearance is largest hole minus smallest shaft: 40.025 - 39.975 = 0.050 mm. The minimum clearance is 40.000 - 39.991 = 0.009 mm.

questions.stem: A hole has limits 40.000 mm and 40.025 mm. The shaft has limits 40.026 mm and 40.042 mm. Calculate the maximum interference in mm.
questions.explanation: Maximum interference is largest shaft minus smallest hole: 40.042 - 40.000 = 0.042 mm. The minimum is 40.026 - 40.025 = 0.001 mm.

questions.stem: A hole has limits 30.000 to 30.021 mm and the shaft 30.002 to 30.015 mm. Classify the fit.
questions.explanation: Largest clearance is 30.021 - 30.002 = 0.019 mm and the smallest 30.000 - 30.015 = -0.015 mm, so interference of 0.015 mm is possible. Mixed signs mean transition.

questions.stem: A hole has limits 50.000 to 50.025 mm and the shaft 49.950 to 49.975 mm. Classify the fit.
questions.explanation: The smallest clearance is 50.000 - 49.975 = 0.025 mm, which is positive, so the shaft is always smaller than the hole. Every pair of parts in limits therefore assembles with a gap.

questions.stem: A hole has limits 12.000 to 12.018 mm and the shaft 11.994 to 12.005 mm. A student says 'the largest shaft exceeds the smallest hole, so it is an interference fit'. What is correct?

options.text: It is a transition fit: C_max = 0.024 mm and C_min = -0.005 mm
It is a clearance fit with C_min = 0.005 mm
It is an interference fit with 0.024 mm

questions.correctOptionText: It is a transition fit: C_max = 0.024 mm and C_min = -0.005 mm

distractorRationale.a: Fit has clearance for some pairs.

questions.explanation: Largest clearance is 12.018 - 11.994 = 0.024 mm; smallest is 12.000 - 12.005 = -0.005 mm, so both clearance and interference can occur: transition. The shaft's largest size exceeding the hole's smallest size alone is not enough to call it interference.

questions.stem: A ball bearing is to be fitted to a rotating shaft carrying a steady load. Select a preferred shaft tolerance for the bearing seat, state the fit class, and justify the choice.
markingGuide: k6 (or similar transition/light interference) on the shaft
Prevents creep of the inner ring on the shaft
questions.explanation: Credit for a suitable fit, its class and the reasoning on creep and assembly. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: A designer specifies H7/h6 on a 16 mm location where H7 is 0 to +0.018 and h6 is 0 to -0.011 mm. Calculate the limits of clearance, classify the fit and explain what zero minimum clearance means for assembly.
markingGuide: At worst parts touch with no gap: sliding assembly, not free running
Zero is the line-to-line limit, not an interference
questions.explanation: A complete answer gives both numbers, the classification and the meaning of zero. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: In a transition fit, depending on actual part sizes, either clearance or interference can result.
questions.explanation: Transition limits overlap, so the actual parts may leave a small gap or need a slight press. This is why transition fits are used for accurate location.
